speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether there will be any restrictions imposed on international travellers entering Singapore; and (b) what are the measures to prevent imported COVID-19 cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These countries should have in place effective systems to test and isolate cases, as well as detect and stop any transmission chains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We will start on a limited scale, focusing on essential travel for businesses to function and for purposes such as maintaining critical infrastructure and providing needed services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: As global conditions improve, we will gradually expand such arrangements to include more groups of travellers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Besides pre-departure checks, incoming international travellers will have to comply with safety protocols on arrival.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These include testing and the use of devices for contact tracing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We intend to progressively expand this list to include other Chinese provinces as well as other countries, taking into account public health and safety considerations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: As a key transport and business hub, it is critical for Singapore to re-establish and strengthen our connectivity with the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We will do so in a safe and calibrated manner, so that we can continue to protect lives and livelihoods.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: We understand that there are some countries that do not have enough test kits and they do not do sufficient testing.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The other question I have is that last month, the Minister for Health did say that we are not doing widespread community testing because the yield is very low for asymptomatic testing.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: To be effective, it needs to be done repeatedly because being tested negative does not reflect immunity and those who had been tested can be infected after the test.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Even if they are tested okay and they come over, they may still be COVID-positive.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We do not just look at one number to decide which countries are safe for us to establish green lane arrangements.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is a holistic assessment of the situation in that country.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Various factors have to be taken into account including their testing capacity and how well they have kept infections within the community in that country under control.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, it is a holistic assessment before we decide which are the countries that are safe enough for us to have these green lane arrangements.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The other countries are making the same assessment about us.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, it has to be a bilateral, mutual agreement before we can establish such channels.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: On Mr Lim's second question, this is why we have more than just one test.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Next, when you arrive in China, there will also be another test done, and pending the results of the test, the individual would have to stay in a pre-identified location.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Only when the test is negative, then that person is allowed to resume business activities.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Other safeguards include not being allowed to roam around on their own, not allowed to take public transport as there would have to be arrangements made by the sponsoring organisation or company.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The itinerary of the business traveller would be something that has to be controlled as well.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, there are additional safeguards on top of a PCR test – multiple layers of checks.
